paper.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: Voyager, an LLM-powered embodied lifelong-learning agent in Minecraft, combines an automatic curriculum, an ever-growing executable skill library and iterative prompting with environment feedback, execution errors and self-verification, and substantially outperforms prior LLM agents without parameter updates.

scope.note: Embodied agent in a 3D game world (MineDojo/Mineflayer), frozen GPT-4 harness with code-as-action, skill library and verification; the body is a virtual avatar driven via a high-level API with perception/sensorimotor control explicitly out of scope. Reviewed as in scope under the domain overview ('controls a robot, a navigating agent or a simulator'); aggregator may reverse to out_of_scope (EVIDENCE lists robot/nav/UAV simulators).

evidence.quote: Voyager, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores the world, acquires diverse skills, and makes novel discoveries without human intervention
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim as written by the authors.

evidence.quote: an ever-growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex behaviors, and 3) a new iterative prompting mechanism
evidence.support_explanation: Names the two load-bearing mechanisms: skill library and iterative prompting (with curriculum as the third).

evidence.quote: these agents are not lifelong learners that can progressively acquire, update, accumulate, and transfer knowledge over extended time spans
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: existing LLM agents do not accumulate skills.

evidence.quote: because we rely on the high-level Mineflayer [ 52 ] API to control the agent
evidence.support_explanation: The body is controlled through a high-level API (pathfinding, mining, crafting), not motor control.

evidence.quote: pushing the limits of GPT-4 for lifelong embodied agent learning, rather than solving the 3D perception or sensorimotor control problems
evidence.support_explanation: Authors place perception and sensorimotor control out of scope: relevant to the EH Radar scope flag.

evidence.quote: Each time GPT-4 generates and verifies a new skill, we add it to the skill library, represented by a vector database
evidence.support_explanation: Retention rule: add on verification; storage is a vector DB keyed by description embedding.

evidence.quote: we perform querying to identify the top-5 relevant skills
evidence.support_explanation: Later use: top-5 retrieval into the code-generation prompt.

evidence.quote: If the agent gets stuck after 4 rounds of code generation, then we query the curriculum for another task
evidence.support_explanation: Local retry budget of 4 rounds before moving on.

evidence.quote: we instantiate another GPT-4 agent for self-verification
evidence.support_explanation: Selection signal is an LLM critic, not a hand-coded or environment success checker.

evidence.quote: we incorporate many bot.chat() into Mineflayer functions to provide abundant environment feedback and implement various condition checks along with try-catch exceptions
evidence.support_explanation: Environment feedback channel is engineered by the authors and shared with baselines.

evidence.quote: These methods are originally designed only for NLP tasks without embodiment, therefore we have to re-interpret them to be executable in MineDojo and compatible with our experimental setting
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines (ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT) are re-implementations by the authors.

evidence.quote: ReAct undergoes one round of code generation from scratch, followed by three rounds of code refinement
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline loop design is authors' adaptation.

evidence.quote: We run three trials for each method
evidence.support_explanation: Three runs per method (the stated reason for small denominators).

evidence.quote: discovering 63 unique items within 160 prompting iterations
evidence.support_explanation: Exploration headline (3.3x claimed vs baselines); budget unit is prompting iterations.

evidence.quote: Voyager is the only one to unlock the diamond level of the tech tree
evidence.support_explanation: Tech-tree result: diamond level reached in 1/3 runs only (Table 1 shows 102 iterations, 1/3).

evidence.quote: Fractions indicate the number of successful trials out of three total runs
evidence.support_explanation: Denominator of the tech-tree table.

evidence.quote: reset it to a newly instantiated world, and test it with unseen tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Zero-shot generalization setup: new world, four unseen tasks, empty inventory.

evidence.quote: 0/3 means the method fails to solve the task within the maximal prompting iterations (50)
evidence.support_explanation: Zero-shot table denominators: 3 attempts per task, 50-iteration cap.

evidence.quote: gives a boost to AutoGPT
evidence.support_explanation: The learned library also helps AutoGPT (plug-and-play), partial evidence for library causality.

evidence.quote: if the curriculum is replaced with a random one
evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum ablation (random/manual) reported as percentage drops in the discovered-item count.

evidence.quote: Self-verification is the most important among all the feedback types
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback-type ablation; critic matters most.

evidence.quote: Voyager w/o skill library exhibits a tendency to plateau in the later stages
evidence.support_explanation: Skill library ablation (also Table 1: no diamond without library).

evidence.quote: GPT-4 significantly outperforms GPT-3.5 in code generation
evidence.support_explanation: Backbone dependence: the harness result is tied to GPT-4.

evidence.quote: Occasionally, self-verification module may also fail, such as not recognizing spider string as a success signal of beating a spider
evidence.support_explanation: Critic false negatives; qualitative.

evidence.quote: The automatic curriculum occasionally proposes unachievable tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum hallucination; qualitative.

evidence.quote: The GPT-4 API incurs significant costs.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost acknowledged; no token or dollar figures.

evidence.quote: We conduct an evaluation of our skill retrieval (309 samples in total)
evidence.support_explanation: Skill retrieval accuracy measured on 309 samples.

evidence.quote: Top-1 Acc Top-2 Acc Top-3 Acc Top-4 Acc Top-5 Acc 80.2\pm 3.0 89.3\pm 1.8 93.2\pm 0.7 95.2\pm 1.8 96.5\pm 0.3
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval accuracy; top-5 96.5%.

evidence.quote: We additionally run new experiments with gpt-4-0613 and find that the performance is roughly the same
evidence.support_explanation: Model-version robustness check, figure only.

evidence.quote: In practice, using a wiki knowledge base is optional since GPT-3.5 already possesses a good understanding of Minecraft game mechanics
evidence.support_explanation: GPT's prior Minecraft knowledge is substantial; contamination/prior knowledge not controlled.

evidence.quote: Tasks that require information beyond the player
evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum prompt forbids tasks that cannot be verified from player state, which keeps the critic usable (design that favours verification).

evidence.quote: If three consecutive subgoals do not result in acquiring a new item, we replan by rerunning the task decomposition
evidence.support_explanation: AutoGPT baseline rule written by the authors.

evidence.quote: Voyager does not currently support visual perception
evidence.support_explanation: No visual perception; text state only.

evidence.quote: its application to physical robots would require additional attention
evidence.support_explanation: Authors disclaim physical-robot applicability.

evidence.quote: AutoGPT [ 28 ] w/ Our Skill Library 39
evidence.support_explanation: Row anchor for the library-transfer experiment (successes 1/3, 1/3, 0/3, 2/3).

signatures.object: an LLM-driven code-as-action loop in Minecraft: curriculum agent proposes a task, action agent writes Mineflayer JavaScript, critic agent verifies
signatures.information: text agent state (inventory, equipment, nearby blocks/entities, biome, time, health, position), chat-log environment feedback, interpreter errors, critic critique, top-5 retrieved skills; no pixels
signatures.operation: propose -> retrieve -> generate code -> execute -> feedback (errors, chat log, critic) -> regenerate up to 4 rounds
signatures.output: executable JavaScript skill and task outcome
signatures.conditions: GPT-4 code quality, high-level control API, tasks verifiable from player state
signatures.feedback: environment chat log, execution errors, GPT-4 critic success/critique
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: accept when the GPT-4 critic returns success; give up after 4 rounds and mark task failed
signatures.persistence: skill library (vector DB: embedding of GPT-3.5 description -> program), completed/failed task lists
signatures.later_use: top-5 skills retrieved by embedding of task plan + environment feedback for every later task and in the new world
signatures.claimed_effect: 3.3x unique items, 2.3x distance, 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster tech-tree milestones; solves four unseen tasks in a new world in 3/3 runs
signatures.failure_boundary: critic false negatives, curriculum hallucination, GPT-4 cost, no visual perception

signatures.object: automatic curriculum (GPT-4 proposes the next task from progress + state, GPT-3.5 self-asks/answers questions)
signatures.information: state, completed and failed task lists, optional wiki retrieval
signatures.operation: LLM-generated bottom-up task stream maximizing diversity
signatures.conditions: warm-up schedule releases state fields gradually
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: tasks must be verifiable from player status
signatures.claimed_effect: random curriculum loses 93% of discovered items

gap.author_gap: Prior LLM agents (ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT, Inner Monologue, CaP) and RL/IL agents do not accumulate, update and transfer skills over long horizons in an open-ended world.
gap.checked_gap: In the re-implemented baselines, ReAct/Reflexion make almost no progress (0/3 on every tech-tree level) and AutoGPT stalls before diamond; Voyager without the library also plateaus. The re-implementations are authored by the Voyager team and are not independent published Minecraft agents (DEPS, Plan4MC, DECKARD are tabulated but not run).
lineage: CaP / ProgPrompt (code as policy) + ReAct / Reflexion (feedback loops) + AutoGPT (task decomposition) -> Voyager (curriculum + verified skill library + iterative prompting)
Minecraft low-level controllers (VPT, DreamerV3) are orthogonal; high-level planners (DEPS, Plan4MC, DECKARD) are the nearest Minecraft lineage

closest_adjacent.name: DEPS / Plan4MC / DECKARD
closest_adjacent.unsolved_per_authors: no automatic curriculum, skill library or iterative planning (Table A.2)

gap.residue: No ablation against an independently implemented Minecraft LLM planner; the benefit of the library versus GPT-4's own Minecraft knowledge is not isolated.
gap.stakes: Gradient-free lifelong skill accumulation by a black-box LLM; relevance to robots is asserted, not shown.
gap.method_response: Add a self-proposed curriculum, a verified code skill library, and feedback-driven code repair.
gap.remaining_gap: GPT-4 cost, critic/curriculum errors, no visual perception (authors); no embodied-robot evidence, only 3 trials per cell (ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers not pinned; whether DEPS-class planners would close the gap is unknown.

claims.text: Voyager obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer and reaches tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA.
claims.setting: MineDojo/Mineflayer, GPT-4-0314, 160 prompting iterations, 3 runs per method
claims.baseline_control: ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT re-implemented by the authors with the same GPT-4 and feedback channels
claims.selection_vs_test: no separate selection split; metric is count of unique inventory items and iteration to milestone
claims.result_denominator: 63 unique items in 160 iterations; milestones in 3/3 runs up to iron, diamond 1/3 (102 iterations); baselines 0/3 (ReAct, Reflexion) and no diamond (AutoGPT)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Against three authors-adapted NLP agents, the full harness progresses much further in a 3-run Minecraft exploration benchmark; 'prior SOTA' is not an independent Minecraft agent.

claims.text: The learned skill library lets Voyager solve novel tasks in a new world from scratch, and also helps other methods.
claims.setting: new Minecraft world, four unseen tasks (diamond pickaxe, golden sword, lava bucket, compass), 50 iterations, 3 attempts
claims.baseline_control: ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT, AutoGPT with Voyager's library, Voyager without library
claims.selection_vs_test: fresh world and empty inventory; library from earlier lifelong learning (which run unspecified)
claims.result_denominator: Voyager 3/3 on all four; w/o library 2/3, 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; AutoGPT+library 1/3, 1/3, 0/3, 2/3; others 0/3
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within Minecraft, retrieved verified skills speed up and rescue unseen tech-tree tasks over 3 attempts; 'w/o library' still succeeds in 11/12 attempts so the margin is in iterations.

claims.text: Each component (curriculum, library, feedback types, self-verification, GPT-4) is critical.
claims.result_denominator: percent drops stated in text (e.g. random curriculum -93%, no self-verification -73%, GPT-3.5 5.7x fewer); curves in Fig 9
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supported for the discovered-item metric with three runs and GPT-4; not shown for other metrics or models.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop Minecraft runs with inventory-state success and run counts; fresh-world test is the same simulator/avatar and task family with 3 attempts and a library from the authors' own lifelong run -> not transfer (needs unseen embodiment/simulator or sim-to-real; EVIDENCE rules 1-2)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a 3-run Minecraft study with GPT-4, a curriculum + critic-gated skill library + execution-feedback loop reaches far more items and milestones than authors-adapted ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT, and the stored skills let a fresh-world run finish four unseen tech-tree tasks in 3/3 attempts (w/o library 11/12); component ablations support the roles of curriculum, verification and library.
assessment.author_claim_kept: first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent; lifelong learning alleviating catastrophic forgetting; superior to prior SOTA.

retention.task_improvement: supported within Minecraft: full system vs adapted baselines (Table 1)
retention.retained_improvement: supported but small-N: library on/off in Table 1 (diamond 1/3 vs 0/3, iron 21 vs 29 iterations) and Table 2 (AutoGPT+library boost; Voyager 19/18/21/18 vs 36/30/27/26 iterations)
retention.improver_improvement: not_applicable: no meta-improvement of the loop itself

G.reason: Specific, important bottleneck (no accumulation/transfer of skills in LLM agents) with a clear lineage and a stated system-level comparison table; but the strongest Minecraft neighbours are not run, the diagnostic of baseline failure is tied to authors' re-implementations, and the remaining gap for embodied robotics (perception, sensorimotor) is excluded by design.

M.reason: Operation, information (text state only), selection rule (critic success) and persistence (embedding-keyed library) are reconstructible, rest on a stated assumption (GPT-4 can write verifiable code and tasks must be verifiable from player state), and yield distinguishable predictions that the ablations then test (random curriculum, no library, no verification).

X.reason: Full prompts, API list, pseudo-code, hyper-parameters (4 rounds, top-5, temperatures, warm-up schedule) and retention chain are given; failure modes and applicability limits (GPT-4, no vision, hallucinated items/fuel) are stated; library conflict handling and the exact run supplying the library are the only gaps.

measurement.reason: Inventory-state results in a live simulator with 3 runs per method, fractions out of 3 and +- on iterations; but metrics are items/iterations rather than a fixed success rate, budgets are in prompting iterations, curves are figure-only and 3 runs is small.

causality.reason: One-at-a-time ablations of curriculum, library, three feedback types and the backbone with GPT-4 fixed, plus the library helping AutoGPT; baselines are authors-adapted and unequal in per-iteration calls, GPT-4's prior Minecraft knowledge is not controlled, and magnitudes are mostly figure-only.

holdout.reason: Fresh world, empty inventory and four unseen tasks give a real held-out test where baselines fail and the library helps; same simulator, embodiment and task family, 3 attempts, library provenance unstated, and no contamination analysis.

statistics.reason: Three runs per cell with +- on iteration counts and a 309-sample retrieval evaluation; no intervals or tests, tiny N, and failure causes are qualitative.

cost.reason: Budgets are equalised by prompting-iteration caps and GPT-4's 15x price is acknowledged, but tokens, calls per iteration (curriculum, critic, GPT-3.5 helpers, embeddings), latency and dollars are not reported.
